correctness.rationale: Take J inside the quotient (the image of the arrow ideal, as specified by Assumptions and scope and used throughout the proof). In the full path algebra the unquotiented e_i J e_j can include longer paths; the opening notation should distinguish these two ideals. Under the stated radical-square-zero scope, the formula is correct. Evaluation of the d diagonal inputs generates k^n exactly for distinct vertex labels, by multiplying coordinate-wise separators for each pair of labels. For a word, nonzero radical contributions insert exactly one arrow input; telescoping against the vertex-label difference gives the difference of the two diagonal evaluations. Thus a radical element in the generated subalgebra has its off-diagonal (i,j) component in U_ij(ker Delta_ij), and its loop components in U_ii(k^d). Conversely, for an arbitrary lift x of e_i within the generated algebra, 3x^2-2x^3 is an idempotent lift since (x^2-x)^2=0. Individual lifts suffice: sandwiching a radical element by lifts gives exactly its corresponding corner. Off-diagonal corners are extracted from commutators, because the vectors Delta_h e_l-Delta_l e_h span the kernel for nonzero Delta, using a coordinate h with Delta_h nonzero. The idempotent lifts have no loop correction: idempotency forces both the (i,i) radical component and every other loop component of x_lift-e_i to vanish. Consequently f_i a_h f_i-lambda_hi f_i recovers the loop input. These span conditions give the entire radical and hence the whole algebra, in any characteristic. Conditional on the labels, restrictions of uniform independent maps to the indicated domains are uniform independent; a surjection from k^t onto k^s is an ordered list of s independent rows, and the off-diagonal restrictions have q^s extensions. This proves both formulas and the threshold, with empty domains/products and the all-zero tuple count handled by the zero rank factors. The source checker was read, not executed; it performs finite unital algebra closure, not proof for all fields. The corner derivation and the maximal-subalgebra calculation below are analytic replay paths.

evidence: The A'(i,j) conjugates test exactly identical labels at i,j, since conjugation is trivial modulo J. In A(i,j,H) a single corner is restricted to H=ker ell for some nonzero linear functional ell. Any unit factors into an invertible diagonal times 1+r, r in J. Diagonal conjugation only scales each corner and preserves its hyperplane. Since r^2=0, conjugation by 1+r shifts a generator's (i,j) arrow component by a fixed corner vector times the corresponding diagonal difference (up to sign), leaving J fixed pointwise. Therefore membership of the whole tuple in some conjugate of A(i,j,H) is equivalent to ell composed with U_ij being a scalar multiple of Delta_ij (all scalars occur as ell(r_ij)). For i=j, Delta_ii=0, so this tests exactly failure of loop surjectivity. For i≠j with distinct labels, it tests exactly failure of surjectivity of U_ij on ker Delta_ij. Avoiding these obstructions yields the frozen criterion; multiplying the elementary independent full-rank probabilities gives exactly P_d and hence N_d and the least d threshold.
